bio: This red-shuttered house exudes a subtle Basque feel, a reminder of the origins of the pair of brothers who own this bistro. The elder of the two draws on his extensive experience in Parisian kitchens in a new take on the flavours of South-West France; the younger brother smoothly orchestrates the restaurant floor and provides expert recommendations from the well-crafted wine list. The dishes change from day to day: butternut squash and sage ravioli topped with turmeric butter, Basque lamb confit served with smoked sucrine lettuce and a white chilli sauce. The simple, bold culinary spirit harks back to the owners' roots....
